pharm: Mixture of water-soluble estrogen sulfates (chiefly sodium estrone sulfate and sodium equilin sulfate) derived from pregnant mares' urine; binds nuclear estrogen receptors in responsive tissues.
quick: Vasomotor symptoms: start 0.3 mg PO daily; use lowest effective dose, shortest duration
May be taken without regard to meals
Reduces milk quantity/quality; weigh need against benefits of breastfeeding
No specific labeled adjustment; use caution
Contraindicated in hepatic impairment or disease
May raise circulating estrogen levels; use prudently
Annual breast/pelvic exam, BP, endometrial evaluation for abnormal bleeding, thyroid function
summary: Conjugated estrogens (Premarin) is an oral estrogen mixture used for moderate-to-severe menopausal vasomotor symptoms, vulvar/vaginal atrophy, hypoestrogenism, prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis, and palliation of certain breast and prostate cancers. It carries a boxed warning for ENDOMETRIAL CANCER (unopposed estrogen in a woman with a uterus), CARDIOVASCULAR DISORDERS (stroke, DVT, PE, MI), BREAST CANCER, and PROBABLE DEMENTIA in women 65 and older. It should not be used to prevent cardiovascular disease or dementia, and must be used at the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration. A progestin should be added for women with an intact uterus.
indications: Treatment of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause
Treatment of moderate to severe vulvar and vaginal atrophy due to menopause (consider topical vaginal products if this is the sole indication)
Treatment of hypoestrogenism due to hypogonadism, castration, or primary ovarian failure
Treatment of breast cancer (palliation only) in appropriately selected women and men with metastatic disease
Treatment of advanced androgen-dependent carcinoma of the prostate (palliation only)
Prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis (only for women at significant risk; consider non-estrogen options)

dosage.d: Start 0.3 mg daily; titrate to response
dosage.t: Continuous or cyclic (e.g., 25 days on, 5 days off)

dosage.d: Start 0.3 mg daily; titrate to response
dosage.n: Consider topical vaginal product if sole indication

dosage.d: 0.3 mg or 0.625 mg daily, given cyclically
dosage.n: Adjust to severity and endometrial response

dosage.c: Female castration or primary ovarian failure
dosage.n: Adjust up/down to lowest effective control

dosage.d: 1.25 mg to 2.5 mg (1.25 mg x2) three times daily
dosage.n: Judge effect by phosphatase and symptoms

dosage.d: Start 0.3 mg daily; adjust per clinical and BMD response
dosage.n: Lowest effective dose; only if significant osteoporosis risk

admin: Available as oral tablets in 0.3, 0.45, 0.625, 0.9, and 1.25 mg strengths
May be taken without regard to meals
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration consistent with treatment goals and individual risk

Add a progestin in women with an intact uterus to reduce endometrial cancer/hyperplasia risk; women without a uterus do not need a progestin (consider in hysterectomized women with endometriosis history)
Re-evaluate the need for continued therapy periodically
moa: Conjugated estrogens act through binding to nuclear estrogen receptors in estrogen-responsive tissues, supporting development and maintenance of the female reproductive system and secondary sex characteristics, and modulating pituitary secretion of the gonadotropins LH and FSH by negative feedback, thereby reducing the elevated gonadotropin levels of postmenopausal women.

absolute: Breast cancer or history of breast cancer (except appropriately selected patients treated for metastatic disease)
Active or prior DVT or PE
Active or prior arterial thromboembolic disease (e.g., stroke, MI)
Known anaphylactic reaction or angioedema with conjugated estrogens
Protein C, protein S, or antithrombin deficiency, or other known thrombophilic disorders
relative: Hypertension, diabetes, tobacco use, hypercholesterolemia, obesity (arterial vascular risk factors)
Personal/family history of VTE; systemic lupus erythematosus
monitor: Thyroid function in patients on thyroid replacement

preg: Not indicated for use during pregnancy. No data with the tablet in pregnant women; epidemiologic studies/meta-analyses have not found increased risk of birth defects after estrogen/progestin exposure before conception or in early pregnancy.
lact: Estrogens, progestins, and metabolites are present in human milk and can reduce milk production. Weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and potential effects on the infant.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is described in labeling; use with caution.
hepatic: Contraindicated in hepatic impairment or disease; discontinue if cholestatic jaundice occurs.

major: CYP3A4 inducers (St. John's Wort, phenobarbital, carbamazepine, rifampin) may lower estrogen levels, reducing effect and altering bleeding profile
moderate: CYP3A4 inhibitors (erythromycin, clarithromycin, ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir) may raise estrogen levels and side effects
Thyroid hormone - estrogen raises thyroid-binding globulin; monitor and adjust replacement dose
interactions.food: May be taken without regard to meals (high-fat meal alters Cmax/AUC only ~3-13%, not clinically meaningful)
interactions.alcohol: May increase circulating estrogen concentrations; use prudently
interactions.diagnostics: Alters several endocrine and hepatic lab tests (e.g., raises TBG, SHBG, triglycerides, coagulation factors); grapefruit juice may increase estrogen levels

serious: Endometrial cancer (unopposed estrogen with an intact uterus)
Stroke and DVT (estrogen-alone); plus PE and MI (estrogen plus progestin)
Probable dementia in women 65 and older
rare: Severe hypercalcemia (in breast cancer with bone metastases)

monitoring: Prompt endometrial evaluation (sampling) for any undiagnosed, persistent, or recurrent abnormal genital bleeding
Regular breast examination and mammography per guidelines
Thyroid function in patients on thyroid replacement therapy
Vigilance for signs/symptoms of thromboembolism, stroke, and (in older women) cognitive change
counsel: Use the lowest dose for the shortest time needed; this is not for preventing heart disease or dementia
Report any unusual vaginal bleeding promptly - it must be evaluated
Seek emergency care for chest pain, sudden severe headache, weakness/numbness, vision loss, leg swelling/pain, or trouble breathing
Perform regular breast self-awareness and keep mammogram and pelvic-exam appointments
Tell every clinician you take estrogen (affects surgery/immobilization and lab tests); avoid smoking, which raises clot risk
pk: Slow release of conjugated estrogens over several hours from the tablet
Variable by component; tmax over hours
Component-dependent (estrone and conjugated estrogens), several hours
Sustained estrogenic effect with daily dosing
Store at controlled room temperature per labeling
pearls: BOXED WARNING: endometrial cancer, cardiovascular disorders (stroke, DVT, PE, MI), breast cancer, and probable dementia
Add a progestin in any woman with a uterus to cut endometrial cancer/hyperplasia risk; not needed if no uterus
Do NOT use to prevent cardiovascular disease or dementia
Increased dementia risk applies to women 65 years and older (WHI Memory Study)
Metabolized partly by CYP3A4 - watch inducers/inhibitors and grapefruit juice
Discontinue immediately if a thromboembolic event, stroke, MI, vision loss, severe hypercalcemia, severe hypertriglyceridemia, or cholestatic jaundice occurs
missed: If a daily dose is missed, take it when remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up. Missed doses may increase breakthrough bleeding.
overdose: Overdose may cause nausea, vomiting, breast tenderness, abdominal pain, drowsiness and fatigue; withdrawal bleeding may occur in women. Treatment is discontinuation of therapy with supportive, symptomatic care.
